question: The platform of an inertial navigation system (INS) is maintained at rights angles to the local vertical by applying corrections for the effects of:

options.text: gyroscopic inertia, earth precession and pendulous oscillation
vertical velocities, earth precession, centrifugal forces and transport drift
movement in the yawing plane, secondary precession and pendulous oscillation
aircraft manoeuvres, earth rotation, transport wander and Coriolis

explanation: The platform must be torqued to stay level as the aircraft moves over a curved, rotating Earth: corrections are applied for aircraft movement (transport rate), Earth rotation, transport wander and Coriolis.

question: How long does alignment of an IRS (Laser Ring Gyros) normally take at mid-latitudes?
explanation: A ring-laser-gyro IRS typically needs about 10 minutes to align at mid-latitudes (longer at high latitudes).

question: On the B737 FMC the FAIL light when illuminated indicates:

options.text: That both FMCs have a total power failure.
That the relevant pilots FMC has a total power failure.
That the FMC test is in progress.
That no IRS information is being automatically fed to the relevant FMC.

explanation: The FAIL light on a B737 CDU shows that the associated (own-side) FMC has failed.

question: Which component of the B737-400 Flight Management System (FMS) is used to enter flight plan routing and performance parameters?
explanation: The Multi-Function Control Display Unit (CDU) is the crew interface used to enter route and performance data into the FMC.

question: ATT Mode of the Inertial Reference System (IRS) is a back-up mode providing:
explanation: ATT (attitude) mode is the reversionary mode: it provides attitude plus heading (heading must be entered manually and drifts); no navigation information.

question: IRS differs from INS in that it:

options.text: has a longer spin-up time and is not affected by vertical accelerations due to gravity.
has a shorter spin-up time and suffers from laser lock.
does not need to correct for Coriolis and central acceleration.
does not experience Schuler errors as accelerometers are strapped down and are not rotated by a V/R feedback loop.

explanation: Strap-down ring laser gyros spin up/align faster but suffer "lock-in" (laser lock) at very low rotation rates, cured by dither.

question: Which of the following statements concerning the position indicated on the Inertial Reference System (IRS) display is correct?

options.text: It is updated when go-around is selected on take-off.
It is constantly updated from information obtained by the FMC.
It is not updated once the IRS mode is set to NAV.
The positions from the two IRSs are compared to obtain a best position which is displayed on the IRS.

explanation: IRS position is not updated once NAV is selected — it is pure inertial; the FMC computes its own updated position from radio/GPS.

question: In the Boeing 737-400 FMS, the CDU is used to:

options.text: manually initialise the IRS and FMC with dispatch information.
automatically initialise the IRS and FMC with dispatch information.
manually initialise the Flight Director System and FMC with dispatch information.
manually initialise the Flight Director System, FMC and Autothrottle with dispatch information.

explanation: The CDU is used by the crew to manually initialise the IRS (present position) and the FMC (route, performance).

question: What can be used to enter positions on all INS systems?
explanation: Every INS accepts positions as geographical coordinates (lat/long); names and range/bearing entries depend on the system.

question: Which of the following lists all the methods that can be used to enter Created Waypoints into the CDU of a B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?

options.text: Identifier bearing/distance; place bearing/place bearing; latitude and longitude; waypoint name.
Identifier bearing/distance; place bearing/place distance; along/across-track displacement; latitude and longitude.
Identifier bearing/distance; place bearing/place bearing; along-track displacement; latitude and longitude.
Identifier bearing/distance; place distance/place distance; along-track displacement; latitude and longitude.

explanation: B737 created waypoints: place-bearing/distance, place-bearing/place-bearing, along-track displacement, and lat/long.

question: One of the errors inherent in a ring laser gyroscope occurs at low input rotation rates tending towards zero when a phenomenon known as lock-in is experienced. What is the name of the technique, effected by means of a piezo-electric motor, that is used to correct this error?
explanation: Lock-in is overcome by "dither" — mechanically vibrating the laser block with a piezo-electric motor.

question: Which of the following statements concerning the aircraft positions indicated on a triple fit Inertial Navigation System (INS)/ Inertial Reference System (IRS) on the CDU is correct?

options.text: The positions will only differ if one of the systems has been decoupled because of a detected malfunction.
The positions will be the same because they are an average of three different positions.
The positions are likely to differ because they are calculated from different sources.
The positions will only differ if an error has been made when inputting the present position at the departure airport.

explanation: Each system computes its own position independently, so the three displayed positions will normally differ slightly.

question: If an IRS fails in flight it can provide:

options.text: navigation information but not attitude information.

explanation: After a NAV failure an IRS can still be used in ATT mode, giving attitude and (manually entered) heading.

question: Where and when are the IRS positions updated?

options.text: During flight IRS positions are automatically updated by the FMC.
Only on the ground during the alignment procedure.
IRS positions are updated by pressing the Take-off/Go-around button at the start of the take-off roll.
Updating is normally carried out by the crew when over-flying a known position (VOR station or NDB).

explanation: IRS positions are set only on the ground during alignment; in flight the FMC, not the IRS, is updated.

question: In an Inertial Navigation System (INS), Ground Speed (GS) is calculated:

options.text: from TAS and W/V from RNAV data.
from TAS and W/V from Air Data Computer (ADC).
by integrating gyro precession in N/S and E/W directions respectively.

explanation: Accelerometers measure acceleration; integrating once gives velocity (GS), twice gives distance.

question: During initial alignment an inertial navigation system is north aligned by inputs from:

options.text: horizontal accelerometers and the east gyro.
the aircraft remote reading compass system.
computer matching of measured gravity magnitude to gravity magnitude of initial alignment.
vertical accelerometers and the north gyro.

explanation: During gyrocompassing the north alignment uses the horizontal accelerometers (levelling) and the east gyro sensing Earth-rate.

question: Which FMC/CDU page normally appears on initial power application to the B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?
explanation: At power-up the B737 CDU shows the IDENT page (model, nav database and its validity), followed by POS INIT.

question: When is the last point at which an INS or IRS may be selected to NAV mode?

options.text: After passengers and freight are aboard.
Immediately prior to push back or taxi from the gate.
On operation of the TOGA switch when opening the throttles for the take-off

explanation: NAV mode must be selected after alignment and before the aircraft is moved (before push-back/taxi).

question: What does the sensor of an INS/IRS measure?
explanation: INS/IRS sensors (accelerometers) measure acceleration; velocity and distance come from integration.

question: During the initial alignment of an inertial navigation system (INS) the equipment:

options.text: will accept a 10° error in initial latitude but will not accept a 10° error in initial longitude.
will not accept a 10° error in initial latitude but will accept a 10° error in initial longitude.
will accept a 10° error in initial latitude and initial longitude.
will not accept a 10° error in initial latitude or initial longitude.

explanation: During gyrocompassing the INS computes latitude from Earth-rate and rejects a large latitude error; it cannot check longitude, so a longitude error is accepted.

question: With reference to inertial navigation systems, a TAS input is:

options.text: required to provide a W/V read out.

explanation: An INS needs no air data to navigate; TAS is input only so it can compute and display the wind velocity.

question: The azimuth gyro of an inertial unit has a drift of 0.01° /HR. After a flight of 12 HR with a ground speed of 500 kt, the error on the aeroplane position is approximately:
explanation: A gyro drifting at a constant rate gives a heading error growing with time, so cross-track error ≈ ½ × GS × drift rate × t² = ½ × 500 × (0.01° in rad) × 12² ≈ 6 NM.

question: An aircraft equipped with an Inertial Navigation system (INS) flies with INS 1 coupled with autopilot 1. Both inertial navigation systems are navigating from waypoint A to B. The inertial systems CDU s show: XTK on INS 1 = 0 XTK on INS 2 = 8L From:

options.text: only inertial navigation No 1 is drifting.
only inertial navigation No 2 is drifting.
at least one of the inertial navigation systems is drifting.
the autopilot is unserviceable in NAV mode.

explanation: The autopilot keeps INS 1 at zero cross-track; INS 2 disagreeing by 8 NM only proves that at least one system is drifting.

question: An Inertial Navigation System, what is the output of the first stage North/South integrator?
explanation: Integrating the N/S accelerometer once gives velocity along the meridian (north–south velocity); a second integration gives change of latitude.

question: A typical FMS installation consists of 2 EFIS and 2 CDU. When the FMC switch is placed in the ALTN position:

options.text: the related CDU and EFIS displays will be connected to the other computer.
the EFIS displays will shift between the 2 FMCs every 30 seconds.
the pilot will be presented with an alternative picture on his EFIS at the interval he selects.
alternative sources of data are used to supply data to the FMC.

explanation: The FMC ALTN switch connects that side's CDU and EFIS displays to the other (opposite) FMC.

question: The drift of the azimuth gyro on an inertial unit induces an error in the position given by this unit. T being the elapsed time. The total error is:

options.text: proportional to the square of time, t2.

explanation: Azimuth gyro drift causes a heading error that grows linearly; the resulting position error grows with t².

question: Aircraft position determined by radio navigation in an FMC is derived from:

options.text: DME ranges and / or VOR / ADF bearings.

explanation: FMC radio position uses DME/DME ranges and/or VOR (and ADF) bearings.

question: What is the validity period of the permanent data base of aeronautical information stored in the FMC In the B737-400 Flight Management System?
explanation: The FMC navigation database follows the 28-day AIRAC cycle.

question: Gyro-compassing in an INS:

options.text: is possible in flight as the gyros can differentiate between acceleration due to aircraft movement and initial alignment errors.
is not possible in flight as the gyros can differentiate between acceleration due to aircraft movement and initial alignment errors.
is not possible in flight as the gyros cannot differentiate between acceleration due to aircraft movement and initial alignment errors.
is possible in flight as the gyros cannot differentiate between acceleration due to aircraft movement and initial alignment errors.

explanation: Gyrocompassing is only possible on the ground; in flight the system cannot separate aircraft accelerations from alignment errors.

question: In an IRS:

options.text: the accelerometers are strapped down but the platform is gyro stabilised.
the platform is strapped down but the accelerometers are gyro-stabilised.
accelerometers and platform are both gyro-stabilised.
accelerometers and platform are both strapped down.

explanation: In an IRS both gyros and accelerometers are strapped down to the airframe; the "platform" is computed mathematically.

question: When initial position is put into an FMS, the system:

options.text: rejects initial latitude error, but it will accept longitude error.
rejects initial longitude error, but it will accept latitude error.
rejects initial latitude or longitude error.
cannot detect input errors, and accepts whatever is put in.

explanation: The inertial system checks the entered latitude against its own gyrocompassing result and rejects a large error, but it cannot check longitude.

question: What additional information is required to be input to an Inertial Navigation System (INS) in order to obtain an W/V readout?
explanation: With TAS (and heading) from the air data computer the INS can compare air vector with ground vector to give W/V.

question: What are the levels of message on the Boeing 737-400 FMC?
explanation: B737 FMC messages are either Alerting or Advisory.

question: Gyrocompassing of an inertial reference system (IRS) is accomplished with the mode selector switched to:
explanation: Gyrocompassing takes place in ALIGN mode.

question: What indication, if any, is given in the B737-400 Flight Management System if radio updating is not available?

options.text: A warning message is displayed on the IRS displays.
A warning message is displayed on the EHSI and MFDU.
A warning message is displayed on the Flight Director System.
No indication is given so long as the IRS positions remain within limits.

explanation: When radio updating is lost the FMC shows a message (e.g. IRS NAV ONLY) on the CDU and on the EFIS map display.

question: The resultant of the first integration of the output from the east/west accelerometer of an inertial navigation system (INS) in NAV MODE is:

options.text: velocity along the local parallel of latitude.

explanation: First integration of the E/W accelerometer gives velocity along the local parallel (east–west velocity).

question: How many navigational databases are there in an FMC:
explanation: The FMC holds two navigation databases: one active and one inactive (next AIRAC cycle).

question: If an INS is switched off, then on again in flight, which of the following applies?

options.text: It is unusable for the rest of the flight.
You can carry on as before.
It will be usable after a position update.
It will be usable in ATT REF only.

explanation: An INS cannot re-align in flight (gyrocompassing needs a stationary aircraft), so it is lost for the rest of the flight.

question: The period of validity of an FMS database is:

options.text: varies depending on the area of operational cover.

explanation: FMS navigation databases follow the 28-day AIRAC cycle.

question: In what formats can created waypoints be entered into the scratch pad of the B737 - 400 FMS?

options.text: Place Bearing/Distance, Place Distance/Place Distance, Along-Track Displacement, Latitude and Longitude.
Place Bearing/Distance, Place Bearing/Place Bearing, Across-Track Displacement, Latitude and Longitude.
Place Bearing/Distance, Place Bearing/Place Bearing, Along-Track Displacement, Latitude and Longitude.
Place, Place Bearing/Distance, Along-Track Displacement, Latitude and Longitude.

explanation: Created waypoints: Place-Bearing/Distance, Place-Bearing/Place-Bearing, Along-Track Displacement, Lat/Long.

question: For an FMS if a SID has to be entered into the route the:
explanation: SIDs and STARs are selected on the DEP/ARR page.

question: Which mode on the CDU of an INS must be selected in order to display initial Great Circle track?
explanation: The DSRTK/STS (desired track) display shows the great-circle track required.

question: What is the name given to an Inertial Reference System (IRS) which has the gyros and accelerometers as part of the units fixture to the aircraft structure?
explanation: A system with gyros and accelerometers fixed to the airframe is a strap-down system.

question: In an INS / IRS, an azimuth gyro is found to have a drift rate. If t is the time since selecting the MSU from ALIGN to NAV, is the azimuth gyro heading error:
explanation: A constant gyro drift rate produces a heading error that grows linearly with time (∝ t).

question: In which of the following situations is the FMC present position of a B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System likely to be least accurate?
explanation: Just after take-off the FMC position relies on the runway update and IRS alone, before DME/DME radio updating is established — least accurate phase.

question: Which of the following lists, which compares an Inertial Reference System that utilises Ring Laser Gyroscopes (RLG) instead of conventional gyroscopes, is completely correct?

options.text: The platform is kept stable relative to the earth mathematically rather than mechanically but it has a longer spin up time.
It does not suffer from lock in error and it is insensitive to gravitational (g) forces.
There is little or no spin up time and it does not suffer from lock in error.
There is little or no spin up time and it is insensitive to gravitational (g) forces.

explanation: RLG systems need practically no spin-up and, having no moving rotor, are insensitive to g-loads (they do suffer lock-in, cured by dither).

question: The Flight management System consists of the following major units:

options.text: the flight management unit and a VOR/DME computerised receiver unit.
the Flight management computer and the Command display unit.
the Command display unit and an INS unit.
the Command and display unit and a flight-planning computer.

explanation: The FMS consists of the Flight Management Computer and the Control Display Unit.

question: VNAV mode will disengage:

options.text: If the MCP altitude is intercepted before reaching the FMC cruise altitude.
If the MCP altitude is intercepted after reaching the FMC cruise altitude.
If the MCP altitude is set before reaching the FMC cruise altitude.
If the MCP altitude is set after reaching the FMC cruise altitude.

explanation: In climb VNAV disengages (reverts) if the MCP altitude is captured before the FMC cruise altitude.

question: In order to maintain an accurate vertical using a pendulous system, an aircraft inertial platform incorporates a device:

options.text: without damping and a period of 84.4 MIN.
with damping and a period of 84.4 MIN.
without damping and a period of 84.4 SEC.
with damping and a period of 84.4 SEC.

explanation: The platform is Schuler-tuned: an undamped "pendulum" with an 84.4-minute period keeps it aligned with the local vertical.

question: Alignment of INS and IRS equipments can take place in which of the following modes?
explanation: Alignment takes place when ALIGN is selected, or automatically when NAV is selected directly from OFF.

question: For an FMS, during pre-flight:

options.text: Information from the navigation database and load sheet is entered into the CDU.
Information from the flight plan and navigation database is entered into the CDU.
Information from the flight plan and load sheet is entered into the CDU.
Information from the flight plan and load sheet and navigation database is entered into the CDU.

explanation: Pre-flight, the crew enter data from the flight plan and load sheet; the navigation database is already in the FMC.

question: Checking and entering the necessary data in the FMS on each pre-flight page is done by:

options.text: Pushing the lower right line select key.
Pushing the lower left line select key.

explanation: Each B737 pre-flight page is completed and the next called by the lower right line select key.

question: Which of the following can all be stored as five letter waypoint identifiers through the CDU of a B737- 400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?

options.text: Waypoint names; navaid frequencies; runway codes; airport ICAO identifiers.
Airway names; navaid identifiers; airport names; waypoint code numbers.
Waypoint names; navaid identifiers; runway numbers; airport ICAO identifiers.
Waypoint names; navaid positions; airport ICAO identifiers; airport names.

explanation: Five-character identifiers include waypoint names, navaid identifiers, runway numbers and airport ICAO codes.

question: The alignment time, at mid-latitudes, for an Inertial Navigation System using gimballed gyros is approximately:
explanation: A gimballed INS needs roughly 15–20 minutes to align at mid-latitudes.

question: For an FMS, when the TAKE OFF REF page is reached, it displays:

options.text: PRE-FLT COMPLETE in confirmation that all required pre-flight entries have been made.
TAKE-OFF in confirmation that all required pre-flight entries have been made,
PERF INIT in confirmation that all required pre-flight entries have been made.
ACT RTE in confirmation that all required pre-flight entries have been made.

explanation: When all required pre-flight entries are made the TAKEOFF REF page displays PRE-FLT COMPLETE.

question: What is the sequence of pages on start-up of the Boeing 737 - 400 FMS?
explanation: Start-up sequence: IDENT → POS INIT → RTE.

question: An INS, what is the output of the E/W second-stage integrator?
explanation: Second integration of the E/W accelerometer gives E/W distance (departure → change of longitude).

question: Which of the following statements is correct concerning Ring Laser Gyros?

options.text: They are not necessarily fixed to true north and are quick to erect.
They are not necessarily fixed to true north but take a long time to erect.
They do not suffer from lock-in and are unaffected by the Earth’s gravitational force.
Their alignment will be either with true north or the local vertical.

explanation: Ring laser gyros measure rotation about their own axes (not tied to true north mechanically) and need almost no run-up.

question: As the INS position of the departure aerodrome, coordinates 35° 32.7N 139° 46.3W are input instead of 35° 32.7N 139° 46.3E. When the aircraft subsequently passes point 52° N 180° W, the longitude value show on the INS will be:
explanation: The INS adds the d.long actually flown (+40°13.7′ to reach 180°) to the wrong start 139°46.3′W → 099°32.6′W.

question: If flying the climb speed profile would cause a violation of an altitude constraint:

options.text: The UNABLE NEXT ALT message appears.

explanation: If the climb profile would violate a constraint the FMC shows UNABLE NEXT ALT.

question: What are, in order of highest priority followed by lowest, the two levels of message produced by the CDU of the B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?
explanation: B737 FMC message levels: Alerting (higher priority) and Advisory.

question: Which of the following equipments does not use information from external sources in flight?
explanation: An INS/IRS is self-contained: it uses no external signals in flight.

question: In the B737-400 Flight Management System the CDUs are used during pre-flight to:

options.text: manually initialize the IRSs and FMC with dispatch information.
automatically initialize the IRSs and FMC with dispatch information.
manually initialize the Flight Director System and FMC with dispatch information.
manually initialize the IRSs, FMC and Autothrottle with dispatch information.

explanation: The CDUs are used to manually initialise the IRSs and FMC with dispatch information.

question: How is the radio position determined by the FMC in the B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?

options.text: DME ranges and/ or VOR/ADF bearings.

explanation: FMC radio position: DME/DME ranges and/or VOR/ADF bearings (VOR/DME).

question: What are the positions (in the order left to right) on the Boeing 737-400 IRS MSU mode selector?
explanation: The B737 IRS mode selector reads OFF – ALIGN – NAV – ATT.

question: Double integration of the output from the east/west accelerometer of an inertial navigation system (INS) in the NAV MODE give:
explanation: Double integration of the E/W accelerometer gives E/W distance.

question: Some inertial reference and navigation systems are known as strapdown. This means that:

options.text: only the gyros ,and not the accelerometers, become part of the units fixture to the aircraft structure.
gyros, and accelerometers are mounted on a stabilised platform in the aircraft.
gyros and accelerometers need satellite information input to obtain a vertical reference.
the gyroscopes and accelerometers become part of the units fixture to the aircraft structure.

explanation: Strap-down: gyros and accelerometers are fixed to the airframe.

question: In a strap down INS the accelerometers are oriented with their axes:

options.text: with the local vertical, True North and True East.
with the lateral axis of the aircraft, True North/South and True East/West.
along yaw, longitudinal and lateral axis of the aircraft.
with the local horizontal plane, The aircraft lateral axis and True North/South.

explanation: In a strap-down system the accelerometers are aligned with the aircraft's own axes (yaw, longitudinal, lateral).

question: The term drift refers to the wander of the axis of a gyro in:
explanation: Drift is wander of the spin axis in the horizontal plane (topple is in the vertical plane).

question: The principle of Schuler Tuning as applied to the operation of Inertial Navigation Systems Inertial Reference Systems is applicable to:

options.text: both gyro-stabilised platform and strapdown systems.
both gyro-stabilised and laser gyro systems but only when operating in the non strapdown mode.
only to strapdown laser gyro systems.

explanation: Schuler tuning applies to both stabilised-platform and strap-down systems (in strap-down it is done computationally).

question: What is the source of magnetic variation information in a Flight Management System (FMS)?

options.text: Magnetic variation is calculated by each IRS based on the respective IRS position and the aircraft magnetic heading.
The main directional gyro which is coupled to the magnetic sensor (flux valve) positioned in the wingtip.
The FMS calculates MH and MT from the FMC position.
Magnetic variation information is stored in each IRS memory; it is applied to the true heading calculated by the respective IRS.

explanation: Magnetic variation tables are stored in each IRS and applied to the computed true heading.

question: Which of the following correctly lists the order of available selections of the Mode Selector switches of an inertial reference system (IRS) mode panel?
explanation: IRS mode selector: OFF – ALIGN – NAV – ATT.

question: The FMC normally has 3 different types of memory:

options.text: Bubble memory, RAM and PROM DATA.

explanation: FMC memory types: bubble memory, RAM and PROM.

question: A pilot turns off the power to his IRS whilst in flight. If he switches the power back on after just a few seconds the effect will be:

options.text: the IRS cannot be used and should be shut down.
there will be no effect and the IRS can continue to be used.
the IRS can be used providing the position is checked.
the IRS cannot be used for navigation but can be used to give attitude information.

explanation: After a power interruption the IRS cannot re-align in flight; only ATT mode (attitude, manual heading) is available.

question: Which of the following lists the first three pages of the FMC/CDU normally used to enter data on initial start-up of the B737-400 Electronic Flight Instrument System?
explanation: IDENT → POS INIT → RTE.

question: The purpose of the Flight Management System (FMS), as for example installed in the B737-400, is to provide:

options.text: both manual navigation guidance and performance management.
manual navigation guidance and automatic performance management.
continuous automatic navigation guidance as well as manual performance management.
continuous automatic navigation guidance and performance management.

explanation: The FMS provides continuous automatic navigation guidance and performance management.

question: Few modern INS systems use a mechanically stabilised platform and mechanical gyros. These components has been replaced by:

options.text: strap down Ring laser gyros and accelerometers plus advanced digital computers.
a digital horizon and gyrosyn true-reading compass.
a combination of rate gyros and True North gyros.

explanation: Modern systems use strap-down ring laser gyros and accelerometers with powerful digital computers.

question: Which of the following statements concerning the loss of alignment by an Inertial Reference System (IRS) in flight is correct?

options.text: It is not usable in any mode and must be shut down for the rest of the flight.
The IRS has to be coupled to the remaining serviceable system and a realignment carried out in flight.
The mode selector has to be rotated to ATT then back through ALIGN to NAV in order to obtain an in-flight realignment.
The navigation mode, including present position and ground speed outputs, is inoperative for the remainder of the flight.

explanation: An IRS cannot be realigned in flight; NAV outputs (position, GS) are lost for the rest of the flight — ATT mode remains.

question: An INS platform is kept at right angles to local gravity by applying corrections for the effects of: i. Aircraft manoeuvres ii. earth rotation iii. transport wander iv. Coriolis v. gyroscopic inertia
explanation: The platform is corrected for Earth rotation, transport wander (movement over the curved Earth) and Coriolis.

question: An FMS is fed by GNSS and by standard VOR/DME. If the GNSS fails:

options.text: the FMS may still be used to provide B-RNAV guidance
the FMS must be switched off to prevent spurious signals reaching the AFCS
the FMS must not be used for navigation

explanation: B-RNAV (RNAV 5) can be flown on DME/DME or VOR/DME updating, so the FMS remains usable without GNSS.
